lessons.title: Story Time: The Snowy Day
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss events in a winter-themed story.
success_criteria: I can say what happened in the story.
I can say how the character felt about the snow.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a winter-themed story, modelling discussion of events and feelings.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about the story's events and the character's feelings.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of events/feelings — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you played in snow or cold weather.

lessons.title: Comparing Temperature
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare hot and cold using appropriate vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can say if something is hot or cold.
I can compare two temperatures.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing temperature using everyday examples (ice vs a warm drink).
lessons.independent_task: Children sort picture cards into hot/cold and order a few by temperature.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record temperature comparison vocabulary — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the temperature of two things at home (e.g. fridge vs radiator, safely).

lessons.title: What Happens in Winter?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of winter weather.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of winter weather.
I can describe how winter feels.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what the weather has been like recently.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce features of winter (cold, frost, shorter days, sometimes snow).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label features of winter weather they observe.
key_questions: What is the weather like in winter?
Are the days longer or shorter?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare winter to another season in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Continue seasonal observation journal from earlier terms — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Observe and describe today's weather with your family.

lessons.title: Writing Winter Sentences
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing winter using adjectives.
success_criteria: I can use a winter adjective.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about winter using adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about winter.
key_questions: Can you write a sentence about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary and sentence construction — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share winter sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe winter to your family using new adjectives.

lessons.title: Telling Time Recap: O'Clock and Half Past
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to tell the time to the hour and half hour.
success_criteria: I can read o'clock times.
I can read half past times.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap reading o'clock and half past times using a demonstration clock.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading and setting mixed o'clock/half past times.
key_questions: What time does this clock show?
Can you show me half past 4?

differentiation.greater_depth: Mix o'clock and half past confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record time-telling fluency — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise telling the time on a clock at home.

lessons.title: Day Length in Winter
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how day length changes in winter.
success_criteria: I can say if winter days are longer or shorter.
I can describe what this means for daylight.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what time it gets dark now compared to summer.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss that winter days are shorter with less daylight than summer.
lessons.independent_task: Children record what time it gets dark and compare to a summer estimate, drawing a simple day/night bar.
key_questions: Does it get dark earlier or later in winter?
How does this feel for you?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning behind shorter days simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observation of seasonal daylight change — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap what's been learned about winter day length.
lessons.home_link: Notice what time it gets dark tonight.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Winter Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read winter-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read winter words.
I can read a sentence about winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending winter-themed words (e.g. 'snow', 'frost', 'cold').
lessons.independent_task: Children read winter-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading winter words over the week.

lessons.title: Number Review: Counting and Place Value
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting and place value skills to winter-themed problems.
success_criteria: I can count objects to 20.
I can represent a number using tens and ones.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting and place value from Week 5.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting winter-themed objects (snowflakes, mittens) and representing with tens and ones.
lessons.independent_task: Children count and represent winter-themed quantities using base-10 blocks.

differentiation.support: Count and represent within 20 with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Record consolidation of place value and counting — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire counting and place value recap.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting and place value together.

lessons.title: How Do Animals Cope with Winter?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way an animal copes with winter (hibernation, migration, adapting).
success_criteria: I can name an animal that hibernates.
I can say what hibernation means.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what happens to animals in winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce hibernation, migration and adaptation simply, with animal examples (hedgehogs, birds, arctic foxes).
lessons.independent_task: Children match animals to their winter survival strategy, recording their matching.
key_questions: What does this animal do in winter?
Why does it need to do this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of animal survival strategies — evidence for SCI.SEA/SCI.ANI links.
lessons.home_link: Look up how a favourite animal copes with winter.

lessons.title: Discussing Winter Clothing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss and justify appropriate winter clothing choices.
success_criteria: I can name a piece of winter clothing.
I can say why we wear it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why we wear certain clothes in winter (warmth, layering).
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and dress a paper doll appropriately for winter weather, explaining choices.
key_questions: Why do we wear this in winter?
What would happen if we didn't?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for layering and material choice

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reasoning and vocabulary use — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.SEA links.
lessons.plenary: Recap winter clothing choices and reasons.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what you wear to stay warm in winter.

lessons.title: Symmetry: Snowflake Patterns
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify and create a symmetrical pattern.
success_criteria: I can say if a pattern is symmetrical.
I can create a simple symmetrical snowflake.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at snowflake pictures and discuss their symmetry.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model folding and cutting paper to create a symmetrical snowflake.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own symmetrical paper snowflake.

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a more complex symmetrical design

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early symmetry understanding — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Make a symmetrical snowflake or pattern at home.

lessons.title: Ice Investigation: Melting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and describe ice melting.
success_criteria: I can describe what happens to ice as it melts.
I can say what makes ice melt faster.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict what will happen to an ice cube over the lesson.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observing ice melting, discussing solid to liquid change.
lessons.independent_task: Children observe ice cubes melting in different conditions (warm hand, room temperature), recording observations.
key_questions: What is happening to the ice?

differentiation.support: Observe with adult support, simple recording

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and comparative enquiry skill — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap what made ice melt faster.
lessons.home_link: Watch an ice cube melt at home and describe what happens.

lessons.title: Winter Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about winter.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about winter, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What happens to animals in winter?
Why do we wear warm clothes?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on winter facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Temperature, Time, Symmetry
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply temperature, time, and symmetry skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can compare temperatures.
I can tell the time.
I can identify symmetry.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of temperature comparison, time-telling, and symmetry.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 20 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time over the weekend.

lessons.title: Winter Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about winter seasonal changes learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of winter weather.
I can describe how an animal copes with winter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering winter weather, day length, and animal survival.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Winter Changes' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about winter?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note seasonal change understanding progress for the term — evidence for SCI.SEA.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about winter with your family.
